content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Define ecology and related key terms
Distinguish between habitat, ecosystem, community, and population

is the study of how living organisms interact with each other and their environment. Understanding ecology helps us appreciate how ecosystems function and why conservation is important. All living things depend on each other and their surroundings for survival.
The study of the relationships between living organisms and their environment
How organisms interact with each other
How organisms interact with their physical environment
How energy and matter flow through ecosystems
Organisms that can interbreed and produce fertile offspring
All organisms of one species in an area
All populations of all species in an area
All animals and plants in Serengeti
The place where an organism lives
Small specific area within a habitat (e.g., under a leaf)
A community of organisms interacting with each other and their physical environment
The way living organisms depend on each other
How they depend on each other
Predator needs prey for food; prey needs to avoid predator
Insect gets nectar; plant gets pollinated
Changes to one species affect others
One organism kills another for food
The role an organism plays in its ecosystem
Two species cannot occupy the same niche indefinitely
Features that help organisms survive in their habitat
Ecology is the same as environmentalism
Ecology is the scientific study; environmentalism is advocacy
Predators are essential for ecosystem balance
Study of organisms and their environment
All organisms of one species in an area
Role of an organism in its ecosystem
Ecology studies relationships between organisms and environment
Hierarchy: species → population → community → ecosystem → biosphere
Biotic factors: living things (predation, competition, disease)
Abiotic factors: non-living things (light, temperature, water)
Organisms are interdependent - changes affect whole ecosystem
Competition can be intraspecific or interspecific
Each organism has an ecological niche (its role)
Adaptations help organisms survive in their habitat
